offense_players (part_*.csv).semantic: the set of player ids on the field for one play
offense_players (part_*.csv).zeros_mean: an empty list would be N/A, not "nobody played"; none observed
offense_players (part_*.csv).chronology: observed after the play; lawful ONLY as prior-game history
offense_players (part_*.csv).retrieval_provenance: nflverse participation release, hash-pinned in nfl/research/inputs
offense_players (part_*.csv).usable_prospectively: YES as lagged history; NO for the current game

pass_snaps (derived).semantic: plays with the player on the field AND the play was a dropback
pass_snaps (derived).zeros_mean: a real zero: on the field, no dropbacks. Distinguished from N/A
pass_snaps (derived).chronology: derived from participation; lawful as prior-game history only
pass_snaps (derived).retrieval_provenance: P1 build_panel_p3.py from the participation release
pass_snaps (derived).measures_actual_participation: PROXY -- an UPPER BOUND on routes run, because a player on the field for a dropback may block

route (part_*.csv).semantic: the TARGETED receiver's route classification on that play
route (part_*.csv).unit: one label per play, for the targeted man only
route (part_*.csv).missingness: 58-64% of plays carry no value, because most plays have no targeted receiver with a classified route
route (part_*.csv).zeros_mean: blank means "not the targeted man or unclassified", never "ran no route"
route (part_*.csv).usable_prospectively: as lagged history only, and NOT as routes run
route (part_*.csv).measures_actual_participation: NO. It is a route LABEL for the targeted player. Calling it routes run would be a relabelling, and it is not done anywhere in this study

routes run (true).semantic: the number of passing plays on which a player ran a route
routes run (true).retrieval_provenance: no source in this project provides it
routes run (true).measures_actual_participation: would, but IT IS NOT AVAILABLE and is not manufactured

offense_snaps / offense_pct (snap counts.semantic: offensive snaps played, and the same as a whole percent
offense_snaps / offense_pct (snap counts.measures_actual_participation: YES for snaps, but it does not separate pass from run. offense_pct is ROUNDED TO A WHOLE PERCENT and P4B already had to rebase off it for that reason

offense_formation / offense_personnel.semantic: formation label and personnel grouping per play
offense_formation / offense_personnel.measures_actual_participation: NO -- context, not player participation. Inventoried, not modelled in Stage 2

ngs receiving (avg_separation, cushion,.semantic: Next Gen Stats tracking aggregates, weekly
ngs receiving (avg_separation, cushion,.denominator: varies and is not documented per row
ngs receiving (avg_separation, cushion,.missingness: high; a weekly aggregate, not per play
ngs receiving (avg_separation, cushion,.usable_prospectively: as lagged history, with an undocumented denominator
ngs receiving (avg_separation, cushion,.model_derived: PARTLY -- expected-YAC style columns are model outputs with an UNKNOWN FIT WINDOW
ngs receiving (avg_separation, cushion,.legally_usable: NOT for Stage 2: an unknown fit window is a chronology risk this study will not take

present-week depth chart.semantic: depth-chart position for the current week
present-week depth chart.chronology: THE ARTIFACT CARRIES NO TIMESTAMP OF ANY KIND (P4D section 2)
present-week depth chart.retrieval_provenance: nflverse depth chart release, no effective time

mandatory_labelling_constraint: The participation component is PASS-SNAP PARTICIPATION, an upper bound on route participation. It is not routes run. Any Stage 4 decomposition must label it that way and may not conclude anything about the value of route information as such. The gap between pass-snap participation and true routes run is DIRECTIONAL (pass snaps >= routes) but its MAGNITUDE IS UNBOUNDED from the data available here, and is not assumed to be small.
